subject: Is it possible to conduct Backward Elimination?

messages.author: 5b386d0f6ed7ab87
messages.subject: Is it possible to conduct Backward Elimination?
parts:
Hi all, 

I am very new to this package, so excuse me if the question sounds to elementary. 

I am using this package to measure which variables affect the survival of the firms. I have filtered some insignificant variables through univariate models. Now when I put all the variables into a multivariate model, the 95% quantile of parameters of some variables contain 0. Is there a ways to do backward elimination in the INLA package? 

Thanks! 

Ma Ho

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Is it possible to conduct Backward Elimination?
parts:
It is not possible to do it automatically like step() does. But (if you
haven't a not to large number of models) is is possible to fit all they.
Example:

n = 100
x1 = runif(n)
x2 = runif(n)
x = arima.sim(n, model=list(ar=0.9))
y <- 1 - x1 + x + rnorm(n,0,0.3)
dat <- data.frame(x1,x2,i=1:n,y=y)

file.res <- 'dic-all-models.txt'
cat('i1 i2 a dic\n', file=file.res)
formula <- y ~ 1
for (i1 in 0:1) {
if (i1==1)
formula = update(formula, '.~.+x1')
for (i2 in 0:1) {
if (i1==1)
formula = update(formula, '.~.+x1')
for (a in 0:1) {
if (i1==1)
formula = update(formula, '.~.+x1')
result <- inla(formula, data=dat,
control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))
cat(i1, i2, a, result$dic$dic, '\n',
file=file.res, append=TRUE)
}
}
}

For many fixed effects, it can be easier (?) to keep the formula, like

y ¨ 1 + X

where X is a matrix with the fixed effects as the columns and appropriate column names.
then you can just change matrix X and keep the formula constant.

yes!

it can be used to reduce the loop levels. Taking a look on the code that
I send in previous e-mail, it still wrong... At each level a new formula
object need to be created as the previous one updated.

Using the Havard idea we have:


n <- 100; p <- 3; set.seed(123)
X <- cbind(1, matrix(runif(n*p), n))
colnames(X) <- paste('x', 0:p, sep='')
s = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=0.9), sd=0.5)
u = rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)
z <- runif(n)
s.z = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=0.7), sd=0.3)
y = X%*%c(-1:1,0) + u + s + z*s.z

round(coef(summary(lm(y~0+s+ssz+X,
                       data.frame(y,s,ssz=s.z*z,X)))), 4)

jx = cbind(1, as.matrix(do.call('expand.grid',
     lapply(1:p, function(p) 0:1))))

file.res <- '~/dic-all-models.txt'
cat('s','sz', colnames(X)[-1], 'dic\n', file=file.res)
form0 = y ~ 0 + ff

require(INLA)

for (s in 0:1) {
     form.s = form0
     if (s==1)
         form.s = update(form0, '.~.+f(s, model="ar1")')
     for (sz in 0:1) {
         form.sz = form.s
         if (sz==1)
             form.sz = update(form.sz, '.~.+f(sz, z, model="ar1")')
         for (j in 1:nrow(jx)) {
             dtemp <- list(y=y, s=1:n, sz=1:n, z=z,
                           ff=X[,which(jx[j,]==1)])
             res = inla(form.sz, data=dtemp,
                 control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))
             cat(s, sz, jx[j,-1], res$dic$dic,
                 '\n', file=file.res, append=TRUE)
             cat(s, sz, jx[j,-1], res$dic$dic, '\n')
         }
     }
}

ddic = read.table(file.res, header=TRUE)
fo = update(dic ~ s + sz,
  paste('.~.+', paste(colnames(X)[-1], collapse='+')))
round(coef(summary(lm(fo, ddic))), 4)
